posts.title: 2D GAA CFETs Need Contact And Parasitic Co-Optimization At A2 Node (imec)
posts.summary:
Researchers from imec published a technical paper titled “Are Gate-All-Around 2D CFETs the Optimal Architecture for the A2 Node and Beyond?” Abstract Excerpt: “Here, we develop an A2-oriented 2D CFET integration flow with a CPP of 36 nm and Lg of 10 nm and present initial demonstrations of several key process modules. Despite their atomically... » read more
The post 2D GAA CFETs Need Contact And Parasitic Co-Optimization At A2 Node (imec) appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Imec researchers evaluated 2D Gate-All-Around (GAA) CFETs for the A2 node, utilizing a 36 nm contacted poly pitch (CPP) and 10 nm gate length (Lg).
The study concludes that 2D GAA CFETs do not offer a scaling advantage over traditional Si GAA CFETs at the A2 node due to persistent contact formation constraints.
Effective implementation of this architecture requires rigorous co-optimization of parasitic extraction and contact design to overcome current integration bottlenecks.

The findings utilize a multiscale PPA evaluation framework, highlighting that atomically thin channels alone are insufficient to drive density improvements without broader process integration breakthroughs.

posts.title: Standards-Compliant 112G PHY for Linear Optics: Driving Efficient AI Infrastructure
posts.summary:
112G PHY IP for linear optics to reduce power, latency and thermal load for high-speed data movement in AI and data center systems.
The post Standards-Compliant 112G PHY for Linear Optics: Driving Efficient AI Infrastructure appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Synopsys has introduced a 112G PHY IP compliant with the OIF-CEI-112G-LINEAR-PAM4 standard, designed to enable DSP-less host-to-module connectivity.
Adopting linear optics can reduce module power consumption by up to 50% by eliminating the need for power-hungry DSPs and retimers in high-speed data center interconnects.
The technology addresses critical thermal management issues in dense AI racks, facilitating the scaling of interconnects beyond 800G.
This development provides a standardized, interoperable path toward future 224G/448G speeds and Co-Packaged Optics (CPO) architectures.

bullets:
Scientists just created female clones of male mice
The sex reversal technique could be used to help rescue endangered species, say the researchers behind the work.
Scientists have deliberately turned male mouse embryos into females for the first time.
A team based in Japan used a CRISPR-based approach to remove the Y chromosome from male cells and create female clones of male mice.
“No one has done this before,” says Monika Ward, a reproductive biologist at the University of Hawaii, who was not involved in the research.
The feat could change the way scientists think about reproduction, says Takashi Ishiuchi, a reproductive biologist at the University of Yamanashi, who co-led the work.

posts.title: Xiaomi EV delivers 31,267 units in July, 39% of annual target
posts.summary:
Xiaomi EV needs average monthly deliveries of nearly 67,000 units over the remaining 5 months to achieve its full-year target of 550,000 units.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Xiaomi EV delivered 31,267 vehicles in July, marking a fourth consecutive month above the 30,000-unit threshold despite a 9.99% month-on-month decline.
The company has achieved only 39% of its 550,000-unit annual delivery target, necessitating a significant production ramp-up to an average of 67,000 units per month for the remainder of the year.
Xiaomi is pivoting toward the extended-range electric vehicle (EREV) market with its new Sky Nomad series, positioning the N90 Max and N70 Max to compete directly with Li Auto and Aito.
Market reception to the new product line remains uncertain, as evidenced by a 7.28% drop in Xiaomi's Hong Kong-listed shares following the initial announcement of the aggressive pricing strategy.
